overview.reason: Establish a concise, interview-style account of the project before probing technical capability.
overview.prompt: Please introduce this project as you would in an interview. Explain its purpose, the main technical approach of using version tokens for cache freshness, your role in designing that contract, the agent-assisted implementation boundary, and the outcome or limits established by the evidence. Keep it concise and structured; this is a communication target, not a stopwatch test.
overview.recall_reminder: Use the supplied project context. Do not rely on exact labels, dates, numbers, or original wording.
evaluation_criteria: Explains the version-token freshness approach in a coherent sequence.
Separates the person's design contribution from the agent-assisted implementation.
States the documented outcome and limits without adding unsupported claims.

areas.unverified_capability: Can explain and defend the cache-freshness contract, including why token changes invalidate entries and how the extra token read fits the design.
areas.demanding_prompt: Within your design role, explain why the cache contract rejects an entry when its version token changes, and defend the extra token read as the chosen trade-off against a plausible alternative freshness strategy.
areas.intermediate_prompt: Explain how the version token participates in the freshness decision and why the design accepts an additional token read.
areas.simple_prompt: Describe the single condition that makes a cached entry invalid in this design and identify the stated cost of checking it.
areas.immediately_higher_capability: Can reason about the contract under competing freshness requirements, state its assumptions and limits, and propose a verification approach that distinguishes design correctness from implementation behavior.

hard: Explains the causal link between token change and rejection of the cached entry.
Defends the extra token read using a relevant freshness trade-off.
Compares the design with at least one plausible alternative without changing the documented scope.
Keeps design responsibility separate from implementation responsibility.
intermediate: Accurately describes the token comparison as the freshness mechanism.
Connects the extra token read to the stated design trade-off.
Does not attribute implementation work to the person.
simple: Identifies token change as the invalidation condition.
Identifies the extra token read as the cost.
Uses only the supplied project facts.

areas.unverified_capability: Can adapt the version-token freshness design when token reads may be temporarily unavailable, while preserving an explicit freshness invariant and verification boundary.
areas.demanding_prompt: Assume the token source can be temporarily unavailable during a cache lookup. Adapt the version-token contract for that condition: state the freshness rule you would preserve and describe one verification strategy for deciding whether the adaptation is safe.
areas.intermediate_prompt: Assume token reads can temporarily fail. Explain whether a cache entry should be accepted or rejected in that case, and give one focused check for the chosen behavior.
areas.simple_prompt: Assume the token cannot be read. State the basic safety choice for using the cached entry and the invariant that choice must protect.
areas.immediately_higher_capability: Can design and justify a bounded failure policy for unavailable token reads, identify when it conflicts with freshness or availability goals, and define evidence that separates the adapted design from agent implementation results.

hard: States one explicit policy for unavailable token reads.
Explains which freshness invariant the policy protects and what trade-off it introduces.
Provides a verification strategy that tests the changed condition without claiming the adaptation was performed.
Preserves the boundary between design reasoning and implementation evidence.
intermediate: Chooses and explains accept-or-reject behavior for a failed token read.
Links the choice to cache freshness rather than unrelated concerns.
Provides one relevant check for the chosen behavior.
simple: Recognizes that an unavailable token read changes the normal freshness decision.
Names the freshness invariant that must remain protected.

areas.changed_condition: The version-token source can be temporarily unavailable during a cache lookup.

model_drift_limitation.reason: Alias identity can drift; each raw response and exact configuration are retained.
